title: Security audit Q&A templates and competitor gaps
summary: Practical Q&A templates and short competitor-gap notes to help sellers respond to SOC2/ISO/HIPAA audit questions, explain our audit-log model, and position Redwood against hosted+self-hosted alternatives.
sales_snippets: Short pitch: Redwood provides a single inference API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with audit trails, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, and role-based access — so customers get consistent compliance posture without stitching multiple vendors.

For security reviews: We produce per-request audit records containing timestamp, model/version, route, token counts, anonymized caller identifier, and policy decision status. These logs are immutable by default and stored in our tamper-evident storage for retention windows customers configure.

Data residency line: Customers choose region-bound storage and shard routing; for dedicated or private deployments logs remain in customer VPC or on-prem storage and can be exported to customer SIEMs via S3/HTTPS connectors.
audit_log_snippets: Template A (quick): 'Our audit logs capture request metadata (time, request id, model id, region), request headers (non-sensitive), and system-level events (scaling, failover). Payload-level data is logged only when customers enable full request logging and is redacted by default.'

Template B (detailed): 'Retention: default 90 days for hosted customers; adjustable to enterprise retention tiers. Integrity: logs are write-once with SHA256 checksums stored alongside records. Access: RBAC enforced via IAM groups with MFA and approval workflows for log export.'

Template C (HIPAA-specific): 'For HIPAA customers under a BAA, audit logs capturing PHI-related request identifiers are stored in customer-controlled encryption keys; access to logs is exclusively via customer-approved SSO roles and audited themselves.'
soc2_iso_checklist: Evidence: SOC2 incoming auditor packet — list of production hosts, network diagrams, incident runbooks, and example audit-log exports (last 30 days)
Controls to call out: RBAC, MFA for admin console, key rotation policies, encryption-at-rest and in-transit, logging/monitoring coverage for control plane and data plane
Operational proof points: runbooks for access revocation, monthly log integrity scan reports, patching cadence (CVE SLAs), and a dedicated security on-call rota
ISO mapping: include statement of applicability, Annex A controls mapped to our existing guardrails (A.12.4 logging, A.9 access control, A.10 crypto management)
hipaa_readiness: BAA baseline: draft BAA with HIPAA-specific obligations, encryption expectations, and incident notification timelines (24 hours for breaches affecting PHI)
Deployment options: recommend Dedicated or Private for PHI workloads; Hosted can work with tokenization/pseudonymization and no-storage policies for low-risk workflows
Technical controls: KMS/HSM integration for key ownership, VPC-only egress, strict audit-log retention and separation, and optional on-prem log sink
Operational controls: designate a HIPAA POA (privacy officer), run HIPAA tabletop incident exercises quarterly, and maintain a HIPAA evidence binder for audits
competitor_gap_notes: OpenAI: strong managed experience but customers often need additional orchestration for dedicated capacity and fine-grained audit-log export; Redwood differentiates by offering the same API across private/dedicated with built-in audit export connectors.
Anthropic/Cohere: competitive on model safety and API ergonomics; gaps often in enterprise-grade routing, dedicated capacity SLAs, and turnkey VPC deployments — areas Redwood markets aggressively.

Cloud-hosted endpoints (AWS SageMaker endpoints): high configurability but requires customers to assemble batching, KV-cache, and operational tooling. Positioning: Redwood abstracts serving complexities and provides audit-ready defaults.

Self-hosted runtimes (open-source runtimes): give customers control but lack the integrated observability, rollout controls, and audit-template support we offer for compliance conversations. Emphasize our 'no-ops' audit posture for customers who do not want to build log integrity features themselves.
negotiation_tactics: If a prospect asks for unlimited log retention: offer enterprise retention add-on and propose cost-sharing for long tail storage while providing short-term exports to customer buckets for complete history.
If customer requires BAA + on-prem only: lead with Private deployment and establish a migration path from Hosted to Private to avoid blocking procurement near-term.
When competitor asks for discounts on compliance add-ons: highlight engineering lift for dedicated KMS/HSM integrations and position these as professional services (limited availability).
